data.gender_notes: Sharvitha is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Sanskrit word 'saraswati' which represents the Goddess of knowledge, learning, and music. The name Sharvitha carries the meaning “Goddess of knowledge and learning” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Sharvitha usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of knowledge and learning and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Sharvitha was an influential queen of the Chalukya dynasty in the Deccan region of India, who ruled from 1118 to 1163 AD. She was the daughter of king Belala II and is known for her military victories, including the successful defense against the invading forces of the Western Chalukyas.

Another Sharvitha, who is also believed to be a queen, is mentioned in the ancient Indian epic Mahabharata. She is the wife of Bhishma Pitamaha and is known for her unwavering devotion to her husband, who lies on a bed of arrows for over fifty years, awaiting his time to die.
